messages:
maria: FYI I'm seeing KV page-table weirdness when paged-attention is enabled. Long chat sessions on H100 leak memory and eventually return garbled tokens. Reproduces on A100 too.

chetan: Can you paste a minimal repro + model + runtime flags?

maria: Repro below (shortened):
```bash
# run with paged attention enabled, page_size=64, pager_threads=4
python -m redwood.runtime.server --model redwood-v2 --enable-paged-attn true \ 
  --kv-page-size 64 --pager-threads 4 --context-length 8192
```
Logs: "WARNING page_table mismatch slot=1023 expected=0x7f3b got=0x0"
Stack (trimmed):
```
#0  paged_attention_kernel
#1  kv_pager_handle_eviction
#2  host_update_page_table
```
Garbled tokens show up after ~1200 tokens and resident GPU memory climbs steadily.

owen: Sounds like a race between pager host-updates and kernel early-exit. Did we change any kernel launch/return code recently (PR 4223)?

maria: Yes -- PR 4223 fused some kernels for perf. Throughput improved ~+8% in short traces, but long-context runs show ~1MB growth per 1k tokens. I captured profiler snippets: "after PR: kernel_time -6ms, but total_gpu_mem +1MB/1k tokens".

kai: On H100 we use cudaMallocAsync / mempool, while A100 still uses cudaMalloc hooks in our allocator. Allocator differences can expose fragmentation/leak bugs. Can you try forcing legacy allocator?

maria: Tried disabling mallocAsync: leak reduced but still grows over long sessions. Also noticed page-table entries aren't cleared on the kernel fallback path when the kernel returns early (e.g., due to zero-length slice). See log: "pager: fallback path triggered, skipping host-write" — but later kernel reads stale entry.

lina: I'll take point. Assigning INF-7682 to track this. First steps: (1) add assert + checksum to page-table updates, (2) add nightly kv-page-table-stress (A100/H100) job that runs long-context chats, (3) instrument exact host/GPU ordering.

infra-bot: Created issue INF-7682: "kv-page-table: race/eviction bug with paged-attn on A100/H100" and CI job kv-page-table-stress (A100,H100). Link: https://issues.redwood/infr/INF-7682

chetan: Short-term mitigation: 1) single-threaded pager (disable concurrent host writes), 2) disable prefetch for context>4096, 3) add a periodic full compaction that rebuilds page table and frees unused pages. These reduce the incidence while Lina digs into kernel ordering. :face_with_monocle:

deploy-bot: Started canary: branch=chetan/kv-compact -> staging. Smoketests: PASS (kv smoke, perf smoke). Build: https://ci.redwood/builds/84211

maria: Thanks all. Leaving open for root cause — my hypothesis is kernel early-exit path + inconsistent ordering of host-side page-table updates vs. GPU writes. If kernel returns without explicit fence, host may see stale entries. We'll add explicit CUDA stream fences around pager completion as part of the debug patch.

owen: Also worth checking page-table layout on different SM architectures: pointer truncation or 32-bit index assumptions could show up only on certain GPUs.

maria: Good call. I'll add bit-level dumps of page-table entries to INF-7682 and run A/B across A100/H100/NVLink setups.

lina: Great — I'll schedule a pairing session tomorrow with Kai + Maria to iterate on reproducer and a kernel-instrumented build.

maria: Copy. Will upload the larger trace + perf outputs to the issue in a few hours.
